questions.stem: What is the primary aim of general vectorisation?
options: To convert text into images
To encrypt data elements before storage
To convert a single action on a single data element (SISD) into a single action on multiple data elements
To translate documents between languages
To compress data so it takes less disk space
questions.explanation: General vectorisation aims to turn a single action on a single data element (SISD) into a single action on multiple data elements, allowing parallel processing.

questions.stem: In machine learning, what does text vectorisation specifically deal with?
options: Converting textual or character data into numerical representations
Converting numbers back into readable sentences
Removing all punctuation from a document
Translating text from one language to another
Storing documents in a relational database
questions.explanation: Text vectorisation in machine learning deals with converting textual or character data into numerical representations.

questions.stem: What happens in the embedding process after text has been converted into numbers?
options: The numbers are printed as a report
The numbers are deleted to save space
The numbers are converted back into the original text
Machine learning and deep learning techniques learn from the numerical representations to produce faster and more effective results
The numbers are sorted alphabetically
questions.explanation: Once text is converted into numbers, the embedding process uses machine learning and deep learning techniques to learn from those numerical representations.

questions.stem: Which text vectorisation method represents only whether a term appears in a document, without considering its frequency?
options: Bag of Words Term Frequency
Normalised Term Frequency
Binary Term Frequency
Inverse Document Frequency
Word embedding
questions.explanation: Binary Term Frequency represents whether a term appears or not in a document, without considering its frequency.

questions.stem: What does Bag of Words (BoW) Term Frequency represent?
options: The order in which words appear in a sentence
The frequency of each term in a document, disregarding the order of words
The grammatical role of each word
The length of each document in characters
Whether a document is in English
questions.explanation: Bag of Words Term Frequency represents the frequency of each term in a document while disregarding the order of words.

questions.stem: What adjustment does Normalised Term Frequency make?
options: It removes all rare words from the document
It converts all words to upper case
It sorts terms by alphabetical order
It translates terms into a common language
It adjusts term frequency based on document length to give a more balanced representation
questions.explanation: Normalised Term Frequency adjusts the term frequency based on document length, aiming to provide a more balanced representation.

questions.stem: What overarching goal do general vectorisation and text vectorisation share?
options: Accelerating tasks
Reducing storage costs
Improving data privacy
Replacing databases
Generating images from text
questions.explanation: Both approaches share the overarching goal of accelerating tasks, though they operate in different ways.

questions.stem: How does general vectorisation improve efficiency?
options: By converting words to numbers for model training
By removing duplicate records from a table
By transforming data so that multiple data elements can be processed in parallel
By caching query results in memory
By compressing text into a smaller alphabet
questions.explanation: General vectorisation transforms data in a way that allows parallel processing, improving efficiency in handling multiple data elements simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a common text vectorisation method?
options: Binary Term Frequency
Bag of Words Term Frequency
Normalised Term Frequency
Slowly Changing Dimension Frequency
All of these are listed methods
questions.explanation: The listed methods are Binary Term Frequency, Bag of Words Term Frequency and Normalised Term Frequency; Slowly Changing Dimension Frequency is not a text vectorisation method.

questions.stem: What is the subsequent embedding step used for once text has been vectorised?
options: Formatting the text for printing
Training machine learning models and enhancing natural language processing tasks
Backing up the original documents
Checking the spelling of the original text
Converting the numbers into a PDF
questions.explanation: The embedding process leverages the numerical representations for training machine learning models, enhancing the efficiency of natural language processing tasks.
